summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, atrial fibrillation, recurrent C. difficile colitis, and carotid artery disease was admitted for acute-onset leg weakness and unsteadiness. Initial imaging ruled out spinal cord compression, but brain MRI revealed multiple acute to subacute bilateral cerebral and cerebellar infarcts suggestive of cardioembolic origin. Echocardiography identified severe mitral annular calcification with possible thrombus, and carotid imaging confirmed chronic right internal carotid occlusion without progression. Given his history of subtherapeutic INR on warfarin, he was transitioned to apixaban for stroke prevention. His tacrolimus dose was adjusted for suboptimal trough levels, and torsemide was reduced due to rising creatinine. He showed clinical improvement in strength and balance, was cleared by neurology, and discharged to inpatient rehabilitation with follow-up planned in cardiology, neurology, and transplant nephrology.
problems: Cerebral infarction due to embolism of bilateral cerebellar arteries
Occlusion and stenosis of right carotid artery
Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, recurrent
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
